mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05) during inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS employment exceeds 5,000 jobs, indicating stronger labor market momentum that boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform the prior 60-day window mean (p-value > 0.05) during strong labor additions.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in HOUST industrial production of at least 2% in a month signals weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >= 2% in the current month relative to prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during such demand contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO supply index below 100 (after 2017=100 normalization) reflects supply-side weakness, resulting in negative S&P 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in >70% of INDPRO < 100 months (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return turns negative as investors anticipate tighter policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive during such rate increases (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% signals labor market stress, which interacts with a rising GDPC1 to produce positive S&P 60-day forward returns when both occur.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND GDPC1 increases in the current month
regime_hint: labor market weakness combined with rising demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when UNRATE < 4% and GDPC1 rises (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1%), a sustained decline in RSAFS demand metric of 10% over two months predicts positive S&P 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for two months AND RSAFS falls by >= 10% over two months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when the trigger is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When supply (INDPRO) remains flat for three consecutive months while demand (HOUST) declines by 3%, the S&P 20-day forward return is negative due to over-supply risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO unchanged for 3 months AND HOUST falls by >= 3% over the same period
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during such conditions (p < 0.05).
